title: Voikov to Stomoniakov, Nr 1883/1188/S, Moscow to Berlin, 1 June 1921 (NARA M316 roll 42, frame 1273)

steps.what: Fetched the OCR of the M316 reels and found runs of 5-letter groups, then fetched the frame image.
The letter traffic to Stomoniakov (2,310 letters, OCR) has Russian letter frequencies with no substitution.
Transcribed the message from the image, 615 letters plus 5 lost.
Columnar widths 5-36 on OCR and first model: nothing clear at 120,000 steps, though width 24 alone beat its shuffled controls.
Width 24, 250,000 steps, 9 restarts, masked lost letters: readable Russian, -3.73; the restarts agree in rotations.
Set Q to the soft sign from desiatq and vosemq, and rebuilt the model.
Polished by moving columns within the row: -3.21.
Item-by-item reading into a coherent purchase list with its own punctuation words and prod sled ending.
Scanned English corpora and two George Wither texts for the key rank pattern: best 10/24, chance level.

validation.notes: Transposition: letters are unchanged, so the token-key test does not apply; shuffled-letter controls are in the notes.

outcome.method_basis: The 24-column key came from annealing against a Russian model with no crib, and gives a coherent purchase list.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decryption.txt, letters; 8 of 615 unread (chetyre shjima, ce)
outcome.notes: Key source unknown. Several letters are radio or copying slips, emended in brackets.

texts.label: Nr 1883/1188/S, 1 June 1921

reading_review.note: Read by the model as sentences item by item; no independent reader yet.

texts.summary: A buying order to Stomoniakov in Berlin: hardware for the goods-exchange fund with the countryside, listed with sizes (iron, nails, shovels, rakes, forks, axes, saws, chisels). It ends "continuation follows". The goods-exchange subject fits the Politburo decision on Kopp's proposal of 16 April 1921, by subject only.

prior.where: GC&CS read other Soviet links in 1921 (Tiltman); HW 12 and RG 457 6707N not seen; no reading of this message found

human: Named the catalogue entry and asked to keep attacking the letter traffic.
